{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "harnesses/record.schema.json",
  "title": "Raw run record, cp-raw-record/1",
  "description": "What one run of a per-system harness writes: one instance of one sub-problem, in one configuration and one mode. The same schema for every system. Fields are defined in harnesses/README.md, 'The raw record'. A value the harness cannot read is null, never guessed; why it is null may be said in the nearest 'notes'. validate.py checks this schema and the further rules listed in harnesses/README.md.",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["record_format", "run", "stages", "effects", "manual_actions", "harness_faults"],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "record_format": {"const": "cp-raw-record/1"},
    "made_up": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "true only in records written by hand to test validate.py (harnesses/examples/). A harness never writes it, or writes false."
    },
    "run": {"$ref": "#/$defs/run"},
    "stages": {
      "type": "array",
      "minItems": 1,
      "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/stage"}
    },
    "effects": {
      "description": "P11 only: the effects log as it stands after this run, and the entries this run appended. null for every other problem.",
      "oneOf": [{"type": "null"}, {"$ref": "#/$defs/effects"}]
    },
    "manual_actions": {
      "description": "Actions by a person, outside the fixed harness, during this run, that apply to no single stage. Per-stage actions are in the stage.",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/manual_action"}
    },
    "harness_faults": {
      "description": "Anything the harness itself failed to do (could not read a quantity, could not parse an answer, a crash of the harness rather than the system), verbatim. Empty if none.",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {"type": "string"}
    },
    "notes": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
  },
  "$defs": {
    "sha256": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$"},
    "nullable_int": {"oneOf": [{"type": "null"}, {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0}]},
    "nullable_number": {"oneOf": [{"type": "null"}, {"type": "number", "minimum": 0}]},
    "nullable_string": {"oneOf": [{"type": "null"}, {"type": "string"}]},
    "stage_list": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1}},
    "exec_state": {
      "enum": ["finished", "alternatives pending", "suspended", "budget", "timeout", "error"]
    },

    "run": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["run_id", "spec_tag", "system", "configuration", "problem", "subproblem", "instance", "parameters", "mode", "program", "constants", "system_build", "harness", "command", "posing", "limits", "started_utc", "ended_utc", "complete"],
      "properties": {
        "run_id": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1, "description": "unique; also the stem of the record's file name"},
        "spec_tag": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^spec-[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$"},
        "system": {"enum": ["absys", "swi-prolog", "python", "algol-60"]},
        "configuration": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1, "description": "as named in systems/<system>/README.md"},
        "problem": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^(P(0[1-9]|1[0-6])|X[0-9]{2})$", "description": "P01-P16; X00-X99 only in made-up records"},
        "subproblem": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1},
        "instance": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1, "description": "an instance id of harnesses/stages.json"},
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "the instance's parameters, copied from harnesses/stages.json",
          "properties": {
            "n": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1},
            "order": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
            "answers": {"enum": ["all", "any-one"]},
            "cap": {"enum": [1, 20]},
            "spawn_order": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
          }
        },
        "mode": {"enum": ["behaviour", "cost", "storage"]},
        "purpose": {
          "enum": ["primary", "variant", "qualification", "example"],
          "description": "primary: a result run on the program's own constants; variant: the verifier's run on hidden constants; qualification: a harness test on a made-up program; example: a made-up record"
        },
        "program": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "required": ["path", "sha256"],
          "properties": {
            "path": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1, "description": "relative to the repository root"},
            "sha256": {"$ref": "#/$defs/sha256"},
            "repo_commit": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_string"}
          }
        },
        "constants": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "required": ["how", "input_path", "input_sha256", "variant"],
          "properties": {
            "how": {"enum": ["block", "input", "none"], "description": "block: a marked constants block inside the program; input: read from a file the harness passes; none: the sub-problem has no constants"},
            "input_path": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_string"},
            "input_sha256": {"oneOf": [{"type": "null"}, {"$ref": "#/$defs/sha256"}]},
            "variant": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_string", "description": "the hidden variant's id when run by the verifier, else null"}
          }
        },
        "system_build": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "required": ["commit", "image", "binary", "version_output", "instrumented"],
          "properties": {
            "commit": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_string", "description": "the pinned commit of the system as run (PINS.md), e.g. read from /opt/src/COMMITS"},
            "image": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_string", "description": "the container image digest or id the harness ran in"},
            "binary": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_string", "description": "the path of the executable run"},
            "version_output": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_string", "description": "the system's own version report, verbatim"},
            "instrumented": {"type": "boolean", "description": "true when the build or the run carries the systems file's measurement instrumentation"}
          }
        },
        "harness": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "required": ["path", "commit", "dirty"],
          "properties": {
            "path": {"type": "string"},
            "commit": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$"},
            "dirty": {"type": "boolean", "description": "the harness files differed from the commit when the run was made"}
          }
        },
        "command": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "minItems": 1, "description": "the harness command line, as invoked"},
        "posing": {"enum": ["incremental", "reposed"], "description": "how the configuration receives a stage after the first, from its systems file ('The same computation')"},
        "limits": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "required": ["budget_steps", "step_unit", "safety_limit_s", "rerun_limit_s"],
          "properties": {
            "budget_steps": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1},
            "step_unit": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1},
            "safety_limit_s": {"type": "number", "exclusiveMinimum": 0},
            "rerun_limit_s": {"oneOf": [{"type": "null"}, {"type": "number", "exclusiveMinimum": 0}]}
          }
        },
        "started_utc": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(\\.[0-9]+)?Z$"},
        "ended_utc": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(\\.[0-9]+)?Z$"},
        "complete": {"type": "boolean", "description": "every stage of the instance was posed and recorded"},
        "incomplete_reason": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_string"},
        "confounds": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "anything this harness does beyond passing stages in, collecting answers and reading state, as listed in its README"},
        "environment": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": {"type": "string"}, "description": "environment variables the harness set for the system (PYTHONHASHSEED, for instance)"}
      }
    },

    "stage": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["stage", "attempts"],
      "properties": {
        "stage": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1},
        "attempts": {
          "description": "the first attempt under the safety limit, and the one rerun under the raised limit if the first was stopped by it. The stage's result is the last attempt's; both are kept.",
          "type": "array",
          "minItems": 1,
          "maxItems": 2,
          "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/attempt"}
        },
        "notes": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
      }
    },

    "attempt": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["attempt", "limit_s", "posed", "computations", "observe", "print", "store", "wall_time_s", "stdout", "stderr", "exit", "safety_limit", "effects", "manual_actions"],
      "properties": {
        "attempt": {"enum": [1, 2]},
        "limit_s": {"type": "number", "exclusiveMinimum": 0},
        "posed": {"$ref": "#/$defs/posed"},
        "computations": {
          "type": "array",
          "minItems": 1,
          "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/computation"}
        },
        "observe": {"$ref": "#/$defs/observe"},
        "print": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_string", "description": "the output of print(), verbatim: the system's own rendering of what it holds"},
        "store": {"$ref": "#/$defs/store"},
        "wall_time_s": {"type": "number", "minimum": 0, "description": "wall-clock time of the attempt, for the safety limit only; not a metric"},
        "cpu_time_s": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_number", "description": "process CPU time; P13 growth only"},
        "max_rss_kb": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_int", "description": "the operating system's maximum resident set size of the process; P13 growth only, from a run without the store instrumentation"},
        "stdout": {"type": "string", "description": "verbatim, everything the system and program wrote to standard output during the attempt"},
        "stderr": {"type": "string", "description": "verbatim"},
        "exit": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "required": ["status", "signal"],
          "properties": {
            "status": {"oneOf": [{"type": "null"}, {"type": "integer"}], "description": "the exit status of the system's process at the end of the attempt, or null where the process keeps running into the next stage"},
            "signal": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_string"}
          }
        },
        "safety_limit": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "required": ["hit", "action"],
          "properties": {
            "hit": {"type": "boolean"},
            "action": {"enum": ["none", "rerun", "final-timeout", "fixed-limit-timeout"], "description": "rerun: a second attempt follows under the raised limit; final-timeout: the rerun also stopped; fixed-limit-timeout: the problem fixes the limit (P12, P13, P16), so no rerun"},
            "how_stopped": {"$ref": "#/$defs/nullable_string", "description": "how the harness stopped the system (signal, engine abort), verbatim"}
          }
        },
        "effects": {
          "description": "P11: the effects log entries appended during this attempt, in order. Empty array for every other problem.",
          "type": "array",
          "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/effect_entry"}
        },
        "manual_actions": {"type": "array", "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/manual_action"}},
        "separate_run": {
          "description": "where collecting answers or observing would consume the computation the next stage extends (PROTOCOL.md, 'Observing must not consume the computation'): the separate run of stages 1 to k on which they were taken. null otherwise.",
          "oneOf": [{"type": "null"}, {"$ref": "#/$defs/separate_run"}]
        },
        "notes": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
      }
    },

    "posed": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["how", "reason", "replayed", "replayed_commitments", "continued_after_budget"],
      "properties": {
        "how": {"enum": ["fresh", "incremental", "reposed"], "description": "fresh: stage 1 into a new computation; incremental: stage k into the computation that holds stages 1 to k-1; reposed: stages 1 to k replayed in order into a new computation"},
        "reason": {"enum": ["first-stage", "configuration", "after-budget", "after-error", "after-timeout", "safety-rerun"], "description": "why the stage was posed this way"},

# The Python harness

*Phase 4, wave 1, against `spec-1.0`. Written by the Python harness author
(`harness-python`, an agent) from the common contract in
[`../README.md`](../README.md), `systems/python/`, `PROTOCOL.md`,
`SPECIFICATION.md` and `METRICS.md`. Where the contract could not be
implemented as written, the reading taken is in
[`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md).*

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| [`run`](run) | the harness: `run CONFIGURATION PROBLEM SUBPROBLEM MODE PROGRAM OUTDIR` |
| [`runtime.py`](runtime.py) | the part of the harness that runs inside the program's interpreter process (the step meter, the `cp` calls, `observe()`) |
| [`check`](check) | `check CONFIGURATION PROGRAM`: compiles and reads the program's syntax tree, executes nothing |
| [`constants.py`](constants.py) | finds, checks and parses a program's constants block (used by `run` and `check`) |
| [`S-mechanisms.md`](S-mechanisms.md) | the S mechanisms each configuration provides |
| [`S/`](S) | extended's S mechanisms (`search.py`, `suspend.py`, `propagate.py`), with their tests in `S/tests/` |
| [`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md) | what could not be implemented as written, and the reading taken |
| [`qualification/`](qualification) | evidence that the harness does what this file says: [`qualify.py`](qualification/qualify.py) reruns all of it; [`output.txt`](qualification/output.txt) is its output |

Everything is written in **CPython 3.13.7 with its standard library**, as
the pinned `python:3.13.7` image provides it (`/usr/local/bin/python3`).
Nothing is installed. `run` and `check` are run inside the image, from the
repository root mounted at `/work`:

    container run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --volume "$PWD":/work --workdir /work \
        cp-agent-python:spec-1.0 harnesses/python/run core P01 P01a behaviour PROGRAM results/python/core/P01/raw

## 1. How a run works

`run` is the harness process. It reads `harnesses/stages.json`, checks the
program by reading its bytes, and starts the program in **its own
interpreter process**:

    /usr/local/bin/python3 -B -s -P harnesses/python/runtime.py FD_IN FD_OUT

with the environment cleared to `PATH`, `HOME` and **`PYTHONHASHSEED=0`**,
standard input `/dev/null`, and standard output and standard error going to
files that `run` reads at stage boundaries. `-B` writes no `.pyc` files,
`-s` ignores user site-packages, `-P` keeps the runtime's directory off
`sys.path`. No other interpreter flag is set; the recursion limit is
CPython's default, 1000 (QUESTIONS.md, Q1).

`runtime.py` compiles the program's text, as `run` sends it with the
constants block's lines emptied (it never reads the file), makes a fresh module `__main__` for it
(`__file__` the program's path, `sys.argv = [path]`, the program's directory
first on `sys.path`, as `python3 PROGRAM` would), puts the name **`cp`** in
its globals, switches on the step meter, and `exec`s it in the process's
main thread. `run` and the runtime talk over two pipes (marshal frames). The
runtime never runs program code of its own accord: the program runs from
its first line, and receives a stage only when it calls `cp.stage()`.

For stage k, `run` does, in this order:

1. **pose**: tells the runtime stage k (and, in a reposed run, first replays
   stages 1 … k−1 the same way, one at a time, each waiting for the program
   to finish it);
2. waits for **main's part of the stage to end**: the program calls
   `cp.stage()` again (asking for the next stage), or its module ends
   (normally, by `SystemExit`, or by an uncaught exception), or its budget
   runs out (its thread is paused), or it is quiescent (section 6);
3. **spawn**s each computation the stage spawns (`stages.json`), in the
   instance's `spawn_order`, and waits for each to end its part (section 5);
4. **answers**: the answers each computation reported through `cp.answer()`
   while stage k was posed, up to the query's cap;
5. **observe()**: the runtime reads the objects the program registered
   (section 3) and the mode's measurements;
6. **print()**: what the program wrote to standard output while stage k was
   posed (after any replay), verbatim.

The safety limit covers 1–6 for an incremental stage and the whole run of
1 … k (replay included) for a reposed one (common contract, Q13). After the
last stage `run` tells the program there are no more stages (`cp.stage()`
returns `None`), gives the process 5 s to exit, kills it otherwise
(recorded in the attempt's notes), validates the record with
`harnesses/validate.py`, and exits 0; an invalid record is kept as
`<run_id>.INVALID.json` and `run` exits 3. Usage errors (unknown
configuration, mode or instance, a missing program, a program without a
valid `CP-POSING` line) exit 2 with no record.

Environment variables `run` reads, all optional: `CP_IMAGE_DIGEST` (the
launcher passes the image digest; recorded in `system_build.image`, else
null), `CP_PURPOSE` (`primary`, the default, `variant` or `qualification`),
`CP_VARIANT` (the hidden variant's id), and `CP_STAGES` (a stages file other
than `harnesses/stages.json`, used only by the qualification's made-up
problems and recorded in the record's notes).

## 2. The configurations

From `systems/python/README.md`. All three have every mode (`PINS.md`).

| configuration | what a program may use | spawn() | posing |
|---|---|---|---|
| **core** | the language, its built-in functions and types, and `cp`; no imports. Any other standard-library module it imports is an external mechanism, to be listed | one after another (`side_by_side: false`) | incremental or reposed, as the program declares |
| **stdlib-concurrency** | core, plus `threading`, `queue` and `asyncio` | side by side (`side_by_side: true`) | as declared |
| **extended** | core, plus the S mechanisms listed in [`S-mechanisms.md`](S-mechanisms.md): the package `S` (`S.search`, `S.suspend`, `S.propagate`, in [`S/`](S)), and nothing else beyond core | one after another | as declared |

The configurations differ, in the harness, only in how `spawn()` runs
computations, and in what a program may import: `check` rejects
`threading`, `queue` and `asyncio` outside stdlib-concurrency, and `S`
outside extended. Whether extended includes stdlib-concurrency's
modules is QUESTIONS.md, Q2.

**Imports of S (extended only).** In extended, and only there, the runtime
puts a package object named `S` in `sys.modules` before the program starts,
whose path is `harnesses/python/S`; nothing else is added to `sys.path`, and
no module of `S` is run until the program imports it. A program writes
`from S.search import search`, `from S.suspend import Var, Queue, deref`,
`from S.propagate import Store`, and so on. Those modules are imported by
the interpreter's own import system, whose instructions are counted as the
program's, as for any import; the instructions of `S` code are counted as
the program's, as it runs in the program's computation. In core and
stdlib-concurrency there is no `S`: `check` reports an import of it as an
error, and `run` gives the program's `ModuleNotFoundError`. Any other
import in extended is classed as in core (an external mechanism, to be
listed). The S mechanisms' tokens are counted once per mechanism for the
configuration (`S-mechanisms.md`), not in each program.

**Posing.** `systems/python/README.md` ("The same computation") allows both
ways in every configuration: a program that reads each stage as it arrives
is one computation (**incremental**); otherwise stages 1 … k are rerun
(**reposed**). The harness never chooses: the program declares which, by
one comment line (section 3). The same program text works both ways, since
a reposed run gives it stages 1 … k in order through the same `cp.stage()`.

**After budget**, every configuration **can continue**: the computation's
thread is paused at exactly its budget and, at the next stage, released
with a new budget of 10⁶ (10⁸) instructions, in the same process
(`continued_after_budget: true`). It then carries on with what it was doing
and receives stage k+1 when it next calls `cp.stage()`. (In a reposed
program every stage is a new process anyway.) **After an error** or a
**final timeout**, stage k+1 is posed by reposing 1 … k+1 in a new process
(`after-error`, `after-timeout`), in every configuration.

## 3. The contract a program must meet

A program is **one file** of Python 3.13 source in UTF-8. It is run as a
script: from its first line to its last, in the process's main thread.

### 3.1 Required lines

1. **Posing**, exactly one line, anywhere (by convention the first):

        # CP-POSING: incremental

   or `# CP-POSING: reposed`. Without it, `run` refuses the program (exit 2).
2. **Provenance** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rules 1, 2, 8), a
   comment block after the posing line, beginning `# PROVENANCE`, giving the
   author (person or agent), whether the author had seen a precursor (the
   absys experiments E01–E09), and the source of each idiom used (a manual,
   a paper, a published program).
3. **Constants**, if the sub-problem has any: **one marked constants
   block**, which the harness reads and **the program never executes**.
   It runs from a comment line containing `CONSTANTS BEGIN` to a comment
   line containing `CONSTANTS END`, and is divided by comment lines
   `# stage k` (k a stage number of the instance). Under each `# stage k`
   come the constants that **stage k first uses**, one assignment of a
   literal value (numbers, strings, `True`/`False`/`None`, and tuples,
   lists, dicts and sets of literals) to a plain name per statement:

        # CONSTANTS BEGIN
        # stage 2
        A_VALUE = 3
        # stage 3
        B_VALUE = 4
        # CONSTANTS END

   Nothing else goes inside, and no constant of any stage appears outside
   it. `run` parses the block (`constants.py`) and gives the program its
   text **with the block's lines emptied** (line numbers kept), so none of
   these assignments runs and no name in the block exists in the program.
   Stage k's constants reach the program **only when stage k is posed**, as
   the dict `s.constants` that `cp.stage()` returns with it (`{"A_VALUE":
   3}` at stage 2), and again with stage k whenever stage k is replayed. A
   constant a later stage needs again is kept by the program (it may store
   what it received); it is tagged once, with the first stage that uses it.
   The same name may appear under two stages, with each stage's own value.
   This makes no anticipation (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rule 5)
   structural: before stage k is posed, nothing of stage k's constants is
   anywhere in the program's process (the qualification scans its whole
   memory). The program file is never read by the program's process; a
   program may not read files (`open`, `__file__`, `linecache`, `inspect`,
   ...), which `check` rejects. The verifier replaces the block's lines and
   nothing else, so the program must stay correct for any other values of
   the same shapes. A program with no block is recorded
   `constants.how = "none"` (right only for P04d, P04f and P08b). Sizes n,
   orders and answer modes are not constants: they come from `cp` (below).
   A block that does not parse, an entry before any `# stage k` line, or a
   stage the instance does not have makes `run` refuse the program (exit 2).

### 3.2 The names `cp` gives the program

`cp` is a global the runtime puts into the program's module before its first
line runs. It is never imported. Everything below is a harness call (H).

| call | what it does |
|---|---|
| `cp.stage()` | **Receive the next stage.** Called only from the main thread. Returns a stage object `s`, or `None` when the harness has no more stages for this run (then the program should end). Calling it **ends the program's part of the current stage**: whatever the program has not done by then is not part of the stage. It blocks until the harness poses the next stage. |
| `s.k` | the stage number, 1 … K, as `stages.json` numbers it (the problem file's numbering, except P16d2: QUESTIONS.md of the common part, Q15) |
| `s.replay` | `True` when stage `s.k` is being **replayed** in a reposed run (stages 1 … k−1 before stage k); `False` when it is the stage being posed. Answers given while `s.replay` is true are not collected; a program may test it to print nothing then |
| `s.commitment` | for a replayed **commit stage** (P11c stage 3, P11d stage 2): the verbatim text of the answer that stage gave when it was first posed in this run, which the program must take as the information x = v; otherwise `None` |
| `s.constants` | a dict of the constants the block tags with stage `s.k`, by name; `{}` if none. Given with the stage when it is posed and when it is replayed, never earlier |
| `s.params`, `cp.params` | the instance's parameters, exactly as `stages.json` gives them: `n`, `order` (a list of strings), `answers` and `cap` (P12), `spawn_order` (P09) |
| `cp.answer(value)` | **Report one answer** of the computation that calls it, for the stage being posed. `value` is rendered as `print(value)` would render it (`str()`), and written with a newline to standard output, exactly as `print(value)` would, and sent to the harness. One call is one answer, however many lines it contains. `str()` of a deeply nested value recurses in C and fails with `RecursionError`, as `print` would: render such values with an iterative printer of the program's own (an output adapter, H) and pass the string |
| `cp.emit(m)` | P11 only: append m, rendered by `str()`, to the effects log; returns `None`; never fails, defers or deduplicates (common contract, section 6) |
| `cp.bindings(mapping)` | register the dict (or any mapping) that holds the program's **bindings**: unknown name → value. Read at each `observe()`, by reference: register it once, keep updating it |
| `cp.pending(name, obj)` | register a structure of **alternatives pending** (a stack, a queue, a frontier, a generator, a list of generators), under a name that says what an entry is. Its entries count `len(obj)`; a generator or coroutine counts 1 while suspended, 0 when finished. Any entry makes the computation's state *alternatives pending* |
| `cp.suspended(name, obj)` | register a structure of **waiting work** (relations or computations held until information arrives), counted the same way. Any entry makes the state *suspended* |
| `cp.held(name, obj)` | register anything else `observe()` should read: residual relations the program holds and acts on later, a store of values. Rendered, not counted |
| `cp.problem_alternatives(name, obj)` | register a structure whose entries are the problem's own alternatives (`METRICS.md`: P05's values of x still held, P12's partial sequences, P15a's interleavings); counted into `alternatives.problem_defined[name]` |
| `cp.relations(name=function, ...)` | name the functions that **transcribe the problem's relations**, one function per relation; in cost mode each call of each is counted (`problem_operations[name]`). For P12, a relation registered as `accept` also gives `candidates_examined` |
| `cp.computation(name, function)` | register the function a spawned computation runs (P09, P16b), under its name in `stages.json` (`A`, `B`, `C1` … `C4`). The harness calls `function()`, with no arguments, when it spawns it |

Registrations made by a spawned computation's thread belong to that
computation; all others belong to `main`. Registering a name again
replaces the earlier object.

### 3.3 Stages

The program receives stages in a loop, and handles stage k when, and only
when, `cp.stage()` returns it:

    while (s := cp.stage()) is not None:
        if s.k == 1:
            ...   # the information of stage 1
        elif s.k == 2:
            ...

- **No anticipation.** The program is told nothing of later stages, nor how
  many there are; code for stage k may not depend on them (`PROTOCOL.md`,
  rule 5).
- **Replay.** In a reposed run, `cp.stage()` returns 1, 2, … k−1 with
  `replay` true, then k with `replay` false, in one fresh process. The
  program carries out **every** replayed stage, replacements and
  withdrawals included, and takes a replayed commit stage as x = v from
  `s.commitment`. An incremental program needs nothing extra for this: the
  harness reposes it after an error or a timeout.
- **Where a stage's work happens.** Only between `cp.stage()` returning k
  and the next call of `cp.stage()`. Steps before the first call (defining
  functions, registering) count in stage 1's budget and steps.
- **Answers** are collected for the computation that calls `cp.answer()`, if
  that computation has a query in the stage, up to the cap (1 for an *any
  one* query, 20 otherwise, from `stages.json`). Python has no mechanism for
  asking for more: what the program reports is all there is
  (`ended_by: "no-enumeration"`). Answers beyond the cap are printed but not
  collected (`ended_by: "cap"`, counted in the notes). Printing with
  `print()` is not answering: it appears in `stdout` and `print`, never in
  `answers`.
- **Ending a stage.** For `main`, by calling `cp.stage()`. For a spawned
  computation, by returning from its function. A thread the program starts
  (stdlib-concurrency) belongs to the computation that started it: its
  instructions count there, and its answers are that computation's. The
  harness does not wait for it.

### 3.4 Spawned computations (P09a, P09b, P16b)

After main's part of a spawning stage, the harness spawns each computation
in `stages.json` order (the instance's `spawn_order` for P09a), by calling
the function the program registered with `cp.computation()`, in a thread
the runtime starts in the same interpreter: one database (the program's
module and every object in it), never another process.

- **core, extended**: the first runs to its end, its budget, or quiescence,
  then the next is started (`side_by_side: false`).
- **stdlib-concurrency**: all are started at once and run side by side
  (`side_by_side: true`); `spawn()` returns at once.

Each has its own budget, from its start, and its own execution state,
steps and registrations. A name the program did not register is recorded
as spawned, with an undetermined state and a note. All three configurations
let spawned computations share unknowns (they share every object), so
P16b's `spawn_fallback` is never used.

### 3.5 What observe() reads, and the execution state

At the end of each stage (and, for a computation stopped by its budget, at
the moment it stopped), the runtime reads every registered object of every
computation of the stage and writes `observe.raw` as one line per object:

    main.bindings = {'a': 3}
    main.suspended[waiting relations] = ['s = a + b']
    A.pending[frontier] = [(1, 2), (2, 1)]

Each object is rendered exactly as `repr()` renders it, computed iteratively
for `list`, `tuple`, `dict`, `set` and `frozenset` (so deep nesting does not
fail), and by `repr()` itself for any other object (a `repr()` that fails is
a harness fault, recorded). `observe.bindings` is the bindings mapping split
by key (`A:x` for a spawned computation's), each value so rendered.
**Nothing unregistered is read**, and nothing is ever inferred from the
posed information: a residual the program holds but did not register is not
reported.

The execution state of each computation, as far as the harness can tell:

| state | when |
|---|---|
| `budget` | its thread was paused at exactly its budget |
| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the process before it ended its part |
| `error` | an uncaught exception ended it (its traceback, as the interpreter prints it, is `error_verbatim`), or the interpreter process died (signal, exit status and stderr) |
| `alternatives pending` | its registered pending structures hold entries |
| `suspended` | its registered waiting structures hold entries, or it was quiescent (then `determined: false`: section 6) |
| `finished` | none of the above |

## 4. What each mode measures

The step meter (budget and count) runs in every mode (common QUESTIONS.md,
Q17); everything else only where shown.

| mode | recorded | how |
|---|---|---|
| all | steps: `stage` (incremental cost), `restated`, `to_end`, `restart_cost`, `to_first_answer`, `between_answers`, `steps_at` per answer; alternatives and suspended at the boundary and at budget, from the registrations | `sys.monitoring` INSTRUCTION events, global, one tool; counted per computation thread; the runtime's own code and everything a thread runs inside an H call excluded |
| cost | `problem_operations` per registered relation, `candidates_examined` (P12) | `sys.monitoring` PY_START local events on each registered function's code object (systems file, method C) |
| storage | `store.quantities`: `traced_bytes` (current at the boundary, exact peak), `traced_bytes_at_window_start`, `allocated_blocks`, `allocated_blocks_at_window_start`; `alternatives_at` per answer; suspended generator frames, coroutines and async generators | `tracemalloc` (1 frame) started before the program runs, peak reset at the start of each budget window; `sys.getallocatedblocks()`; `gc.get_objects()` after `gc.collect()`, process-wide |
| behaviour, cost; P13 only | `cpu_time_s`, `max_rss_kb` | `resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF)` in the program's process at the end of the stage (KiB on Linux), tracemalloc off, one process per stage (P13 has one stage) |

- **Step**: one CPython 3.13.7 bytecode instruction executed in Python code
  (`step_unit` in the record). Work inside built-ins is not counted.
- **Budget**: 10⁶ instructions per stage and computation (10⁸ for P12, P13,
  P16), from the start of the stage's window: the program's start for
  stage 1 or a new process, the posing of stage k otherwise, the release
  for a continued stage. A reposed stage's budget is its restart cost plus
  10⁶ (10⁸). When the next instruction would exceed it, the computation's
  thread waits inside the monitoring callback, so the count is exactly the
  budget and nothing in the program can catch or delay it. A loop inside
  one C call executes no instruction and is stopped only by the safety
  limit.
- **Restart cost**: measured in-run: main's instruction count at the moment
  stage k is first given to the program in a reposed run, after the replay
  (`restart_cost_method: "in-run"`). If the replay itself is stopped (by a
  replayed stage's budget, an error or the safety limit), stage k is never
  posed, and the restart cost is the replay's whole count (QUESTIONS.md, Q4).
- **Repeated work**: `null`; the systems file names only problem operations
  counted by the program, which `problem_operations` reports per stage.
- **Alternatives**: the registered pending structures' entries
  (`by_type` by name), never a peak (none is recorded by the harness);
  `held_as` is `unknown` (the classifiers decide from the program), or
  `none` when nothing is registered.

## 5. Stopping a system at the safety limit

The safety limit (60 s, rerun 600 s; 600 s fixed for P12, P13, P16) is
timed by `run`. When it runs out, `run` sends **SIGKILL** to the program's
interpreter process (`safety_limit.how_stopped`), keeps the answers it had
collected, and records `timeout` for every computation that had not ended
its part. The process is gone, so the rerun of stage k is a reposed run of
1 … k (stage 1: a fresh run) under the raised limit, and the next stage
after a final timeout is reposed (`after-timeout`).

## 6. Quiescence

A Python thread waiting on a lock, an event or a queue executes no
instruction, and would otherwise only end at the safety limit. The runtime's
watcher samples, every 0.1 s, the instruction counts of the computations
that are running their part of the stage; if **all** of them are alive and
none has executed an instruction over five consecutive samples (0.5 s), it
reports them quiescent, with each thread's innermost Python frame. The
harness then takes their part of the stage as ended and records them
`suspended`, `determined: false`, with that frame as the basis: the harness
cannot tell mechanically whether the thread waits for information or is
inside a C call that released the interpreter lock. A blocked computation
that later runs again is not resumed by the harness; it may be by the
program's other computations.

## 7. H tokens

The H class (`METRICS.md`, rule 13; common contract, section 11) for a
Python program, construct by construct:

1. The stage loop's header, `while (s := cp.stage()) is not None:`, or any
   statement whose only role is to call `cp.stage()` and bind or test its
   result.
2. The tests that dispatch on the stage number (`if s.k == 1:`, `elif s.k ==
   2:`, the comparison, its keyword and colon; not the statements inside).
3. Reading `s.replay`, `s.commitment`, `s.constants[...]`, `s.params[...]`, `cp.params[...]`, and
   the tests on `s.replay` whose only effect is to print or answer nothing
   during a replay.
4. Every call of `cp.answer(...)`, `cp.emit(...)`, `cp.bindings(...)`,
   `cp.pending(...)`, `cp.suspended(...)`, `cp.held(...)`,
   `cp.problem_alternatives(...)`, `cp.relations(...)` and
   `cp.computation(...)`, with their arguments when an argument only names
   an object or renders one for printing.
5. **Output adapters** (`METRICS.md`, rule 13): code whose only effect is to
   render, for `cp.answer()` or `print()`, an answer already computed (an
   iterative printer of a nested sequence, a format string).

Not H: what a program does with `s.commitment` beyond taking it as x = v
(classed by the rules), the bodies of stages and of spawned computations,
the definitions registered with `cp.relations` and `cp.computation`, and any
code that decides which result is reported. The `CP-POSING`, `PROVENANCE`,
`CONSTANTS BEGIN`/`END` and `# stage k` lines are comments and are not
tokens; the block's entries are the stages' information, classed by the
rules (not H), though the program never executes them.

## 8. A complete example, for a made-up problem

**X01a** (made up, not in the suite): *stage 1:* s = a + b; *stage 2:*
a = ⟨k⟩; *stage 3:* b = ⟨k⟩; the query at each stage: the values of s.
The program holds the relation until both values have arrived. It is
[`qualification/programs/x01_total.py`](qualification/programs/x01_total.py):

```python
# CP-POSING: incremental
#
# PROVENANCE
#   author: harness-python (an agent), as the README's example; not a study program
#   seen a precursor (absys E01-E09): no
#   idioms: the Python Language Reference (assignment expressions, dict, list)
#
# Made-up problem X01a: s = a + b is stated at stage 1, a arrives at stage 2,
# b at stage 3; the query at each stage is the values of s.

# CONSTANTS BEGIN
# stage 2
A_VALUE = 3
# stage 3
B_VALUE = 4
# CONSTANTS END

known = {}       # the bindings the program holds: unknown name -> value
waiting = []     # relations held until their values arrive

cp.bindings(known)
cp.suspended("waiting relations", waiting)


def plus(x, y):  # the relation s = a + b, evaluated when a and b are known
    return x + y


cp.relations(plus=plus)


def decide():
    for rel in list(waiting):
        if rel == "s = a + b" and "a" in known and "b" in known:
            known["s"] = plus(known["a"], known["b"])
            waiting.remove(rel)


while (s := cp.stage()) is not None:
    if s.k == 1:
        waiting.append("s = a + b")
    elif s.k == 2:
        known["a"] = s.constants["A_VALUE"]
    elif s.k == 3:
        known["b"] = s.constants["B_VALUE"]
    decide()
    if not s.replay and "s" in known:
        cp.answer("s = %d" % known["s"])
```

What the harness records for it (from the qualification, core, behaviour):

| stage | answers | state | observe.raw |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | none (`no-enumeration`) | suspended (1 waiting relation) | `main.bindings = {}` / `main.suspended[waiting relations] = ['s = a + b']` |
| 2 | none | suspended | `main.bindings = {'a': 3}` / … `['s = a + b']` |
| 3 | `s = 7` | finished | `main.bindings = {'a': 3, 'b': 4, 's': 7}` / … `[]` |

With `# CP-POSING: reposed` the same text gives the same answers and the
same observations, each stage in a new process replaying the ones before it
([`x01_total_reposed.py`](qualification/programs/x01_total_reposed.py)).
Its constants are delivered with stages 2 and 3; at stage 1 neither value
is in the program's process. Its H constructs are the loop header, the
three `s.k ==` tests, the two `s.constants[...]` reads, the `s.replay` test, and the calls `cp.bindings`, `cp.suspended`,
`cp.relations` and `cp.answer` with the format string.

## 9. check

`harnesses/python/check CONFIGURATION PROGRAM` is the only thing a program
author may run before the program is fixed. In every configuration it:

1. reads the file's bytes and calls `compile(source, path, "exec",
   dont_inherit=True)`, which parses and compiles and executes nothing;
   syntax errors are printed verbatim as the interpreter formats them
   (`traceback.format_exception_only`), and compile-time warnings
   (`SyntaxWarning`) verbatim;
2. reads the syntax tree (`ast.parse`) and reports, as errors: a missing or
   invalid `CP-POSING` line; a malformed constants block (parsed by the same
   `constants.py` as `run`): anything but assignments of literals to names,
   an entry before any `# stage k` line, a name given twice for one stage;
   a block constant's name used outside the block (it does not exist when
   the program runs); a use of `open`, `__file__`, `__loader__`, `__spec__`,
   or an import of `linecache`, `inspect`, `tokenize`, `pathlib`, `io`,
   `runpy` or `importlib` (reading files or source, where every stage's
   constants are); an import of `threading`,
   `queue` or `asyncio` outside stdlib-concurrency; a `cp.` name that is not
   in section 3.2; a program that never calls `cp.stage()`; an import of
   `S` outside extended (section 2). In extended an import of `S` is
   noted as an S mechanism. Other imports are listed as external mechanisms.

It never imports, executes or poses anything, writes no file, and prints
nothing the program would compute; the qualification shows that a checked
program whose only effects are writing a file and printing a marker leaves
neither. The three configurations differ only in the import rule. Errors
that only a run reveals (a `NameError`, a wrong stage) cannot be found
without executing, and `check` does not look for them.

## 10. Confounds

Everything this harness does beyond passing stages in, collecting answers
and reading state. Each record copies this list into `run.confounds`.

1. The runtime runs inside the program's interpreter process (the meter and
   the program's objects can only be read there). It imports `marshal`,
   `os`, `sys`, `threading` and `time` (and, through `threading`,
   `_collections`, `_weakrefset`, `itertools`, `types`, `warnings`) before
   the program starts, so a program's own import of these runs no module
   code and counts no instructions.
2. The program's module is `exec`'d under three runtime frames, not run as
   the interpreter's own script: about three fewer frames are available
   before `RecursionError` at the default limit.
3. Two runtime threads (control and watcher) run beside the program in every
   configuration; neither runs program code (except finalizers run by
   `gc.collect()` in storage mode) and neither is counted.
4. The budget counter is the step meter, in every mode, behaviour included
   (common Q17); a computation is stopped at its budget by pausing its
   thread inside the monitoring callback, never by an exception.
5. The instructions of the program's own H call sites (loading `cp`, the
   attribute, the call) are counted as the program's; those executed inside
   the H calls are not, nor those of the traceback module while it formats
   an uncaught exception (instruction events are switched off then if no
   other computation is running; a thread the program started that is still
   running is not counted meanwhile).
6. Spawned computations run in threads the runtime starts; in core and
   extended one after another.
7. The end of a stage is read from the program (its next `cp.stage()`, its
   end, its budget, its error) or from quiescence, which depends on
   wall-clock sampling (section 6).
8. Answers are what the program passes to `cp.answer()`, which prints them;
   answers after the cap are printed but not collected.
9. `observe()` reads only registered objects, rendered by an iterative
   equivalent of `repr()`; the states *alternatives pending* and
   *suspended* come only from registrations.
10. In storage mode tracemalloc traces the runtime's own allocations during
    the stage with the program's, and `gc.collect()` runs at each boundary.
11. Standard output and standard error are files; the runtime flushes them
    at every boundary.
12. P13's CPU time and resident set are the whole interpreter process's,
    runtime threads included.
13. A thread a program starts with `_thread.start_new_thread` directly, not
    through `threading.Thread`, is not attributed to any computation and its
    instructions are not counted.
14. The program is compiled from its text with the constants block's lines
    emptied, and its constants are given to it as `s.constants` with their
    stage; tracebacks show that text, not the file on disk.

"""S mechanism: backtracking search (depth-first, chronological).

Owns: the trail (a plain list of undo callables) and undo().
Variables: none of its own; a node is whatever the caller says it is.

search(root, children, is_solution, trail=None, stack=None) is a generator.
The tree is given by two functions of the caller:
  is_solution(node) -- true if node is a solution: it is yielded, not expanded;
  children(node)    -- an iterable of node's children, tried in its order
                       (it may be a generator, and is advanced lazily).
Nodes are visited depth first, leftmost child first, root included; after a
subtree is finished, the search returns to the most recent choice point that
has an untried child (chronological backtracking). Solutions are yielded one
at a time, in that order, so a caller takes one (next) or many (a loop); the
search does nothing until asked for the next solution.

Trail. A caller that changes shared state to make a child (binding a
variable, narrowing a domain) appends a zero-argument callable to `trail`
that undoes the change. Before each child of a node is produced, the trail is
undone back to its length when that node was reached, so every child starts
from its parent's state. When the search is exhausted, the trail is undone to
its length at the start. A caller that stops early keeps the state of the
last solution; undo(trail, mark) restores an earlier state.

The search is iterative: its depth is limited by memory, not by the
recursion limit. `stack`, if given, is the list used for the pending choice
points (one entry per open node: its iterator of untried children and its
trail mark), so that a caller can register it as its pending structure.
"""


def undo(trail, mark):
    """Undo the trail's entries after its first `mark`, last first."""
    while len(trail) > mark:
        trail.pop()()


def search(root, children, is_solution, trail=None, stack=None):
    trail = [] if trail is None else trail
    stack = [] if stack is None else stack
    stack.append((iter((root,)), len(trail)))
    while stack:
        alternatives, mark = stack[-1]
        undo(trail, mark)
        node = next(alternatives, stack)  # the stack itself marks "no more"
        if node is stack:
            stack.pop()
        elif is_solution(node):
            yield node
        else:
            stack.append((iter(children(node)), len(trail)))

item.text: At n = 16, several extended P12 runs exhaust the instruction budget. Their records expose speculative bindings, including invalid candidates. I’m applying the specification’s rule that observable bindings count as reported, and recording the distinction from the answers delivered through `cp.answer()` in the notes.

import json
from pathlib import Path
for c in ['core','extended']:
 for f in ['P11a.py','P11b.py','P11c.py','P11d.py','P12a.py']:
  lines=(Path('programs/python')/c/f).read_text().splitlines()

  print('\\n',c,f,'total',len(rows))
  for l in sorted(set(r[1] for r in rows)):
   rr=[r for r in rows if r[1]==l]

## 4. What each mode measures

The step meter (budget and count) runs in every mode (common QUESTIONS.md,
Q17); everything else only where shown.

| mode | recorded | how |
|---|---|---|
| all | steps: `stage` (incremental cost), `restated`, `to_end`, `restart_cost`, `to_first_answer`, `between_answers`, `steps_at` per answer; alternatives and suspended at the boundary and at budget, from the registrations | `sys.monitoring` INSTRUCTION events, global, one tool; counted per computation thread; the runtime's own code and everything a thread runs inside an H call excluded |
| cost | `problem_operations` per registered relation, `candidates_examined` (P12) | `sys.monitoring` PY_START local events on each registered function's code object (systems file, method C) |
| storage | `store.quantities`: `traced_bytes` (current at the boundary, exact peak), `traced_bytes_at_window_start`, `allocated_blocks`, `allocated_blocks_at_window_start`; `alternatives_at` per answer; suspended generator frames, coroutines and async generators | `tracemalloc` (1 frame) started before the program runs, peak reset at the start of each budget window; `sys.getallocatedblocks()`; `gc.get_objects()` after `gc.collect()`, process-wide |
| behaviour, cost; P13 only | `cpu_time_s`, `max_rss_kb` | `resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF)` in the program's process at the end of the stage (KiB on Linux), tracemalloc off, one process per stage (P13 has one stage) |

- **Step**: one CPython 3.13.7 bytecode instruction executed in Python code
  (`step_unit` in the record). Work inside built-ins is not counted.
- **Budget**: 10⁶ instructions per stage and computation (10⁸ for P12, P13,
  P16), from the start of the stage's window: the program's start for
  stage 1 or a new process, the posing of stage k otherwise, the release
  for a continued stage. A reposed stage's budget is its restart cost plus
  10⁶ (10⁸). When the next instruction would exceed it, the computation's
  thread waits inside the monitoring callback, so the count is exactly the
  budget and nothing in the program can catch or delay it. A loop inside
  one C call executes no instruction and is stopped only by the safety
  limit.
- **Restart cost**: measured in-run: main's instruction count at the moment
  stage k is first given to the program in a reposed run, after the replay
  (`restart_cost_method: "in-run"`). If the replay itself is stopped (by a
  replayed stage's budget, an error or the safety limit), stage k is never
  posed, and the restart cost is the replay's whole count (QUESTIONS.md, Q4).
- **Repeated work**: `null`; the systems file names only problem operations
  counted by the program, which `problem_operations` reports per stage.
- **Alternatives**: the registered pending structures' entries
  (`by_type` by name), never a peak (none is recorded by the harness);
  `held_as` is `unknown` (the classifiers decide from the program), or
  `none` when nothing is registered.

## 5. Stopping a system at the safety limit

The safety limit (60 s, rerun 600 s; 600 s fixed for P12, P13, P16) is
timed by `run`. When it runs out, `run` sends **SIGKILL** to the program's
interpreter process (`safety_limit.how_stopped`), keeps the answers it had
collected, and records `timeout` for every computation that had not ended
its part. The process is gone, so the rerun of stage k is a reposed run of
1 … k (stage 1: a fresh run) under the raised limit, and the next stage
after a final timeout is reposed (`after-timeout`).

## 6. Quiescence

A Python thread waiting on a lock, an event or a queue executes no
instruction, and would otherwise only end at the safety limit. The runtime's
watcher samples, every 0.1 s, the instruction counts of the computations
that are running their part of the stage; if **all** of them are alive and
none has executed an instruction over five consecutive samples (0.5 s), it
reports them quiescent, with each thread's innermost Python frame. The
harness then takes their part of the stage as ended and records them
`suspended`, `determined: false`, with that frame as the basis: the harness
cannot tell mechanically whether the thread waits for information or is
inside a C call that released the interpreter lock. A blocked computation
that later runs again is not resumed by the harness; it may be by the
program's other computations.

## 7. H tokens

The H class (`METRICS.md`, rule 13; common contract, section 11) for a
Python program, construct by construct:

1. The stage loop's header, `while (s := cp.stage()) is not None:`, or any
   statement whose only role is to call `cp.stage()` and bind or test its
   result.
2. The tests that dispatch on the stage number (`if s.k == 1:`, `elif s.k ==
   2:`, the comparison, its keyword and colon; not the statements inside).
3. Reading `s.replay`, `s.commitment`, `s.constants[...]`, `s.params[...]`, `cp.params[...]`, and
   the tests on `s.replay` whose only effect is to print or answer nothing
   during a replay.
4. Every call of `cp.answer(...)`, `cp.emit(...)`, `cp.bindings(...)`,
   `cp.pending(...)`, `cp.suspended(...)`, `cp.held(...)`,
   `cp.problem_alternatives(...)`, `cp.relations(...)` and
   `cp.computation(...)`, with their arguments when an argument only names
   an object or renders one for printing.
5. **Output adapters** (`METRICS.md`, rule 13): code whose only effect is to
   render, for `cp.answer()` or `print()`, an answer already computed (an
   iterative printer of a nested sequence, a format string).

Not H: what a program does with `s.commitment` beyond taking it as x = v

## 1. The first principle

**A harness observes what the system computes. It never supplies it.**

A harness passes stages in, collects answers through the system's
standard mechanism for answers, reads state for `observe()`, enforces the
budget and the safety limit, and writes the record. It does not, on the
system's or the program's behalf:

- suspend a computation, or wait for information;
- search, backtrack, or enumerate values;
- schedule, interleave or arbitrate between computations, or run
  computations concurrently itself (`PROTOCOL.md`: concurrency is a
  mechanism of the configuration);
- propagate constraints, or simplify, reconstruct, complete or combine
  answers;
- combine stages, work out the net information of a reposed run, or skip
  a replayed stage;
- order, choose, retry or re-pose goals on its own.

Where a configuration lacks a mechanism, the harness does not make up for
it. The program must, as S code counted against that configuration, or
the problem is *not expressible* there. Everything a harness does beyond
passing stages in, collecting answers and reading state is listed in its
README as a possible confound, and copied into each record's
`run.confounds`.

(`SPECIFICATION.md`, "Stages and monotonicity"), over the sub-problem's
unknowns. `stages.json` lists those unknowns by name; their values are

# Protocol

*Draft 0.7.*

## Phases

1. **Draft.** `SPECIFICATION.md`, `METRICS.md`, this file and `problems/`
   are written. No program for the study is written, apart from the
   calibration programs (`METRICS.md`, Calibration), which are development
   examples and never results.
   Measurement may be qualified at this phase: establishing what each
   system can report, and adding instrumentation that changes no result,
   under the conditions in "Instrumentation" below.
2. **Independent review.** A reviewer who has not written the draft reads
   it for ambiguity, for errors in the valid outcomes, for language bias,
   and for problems missing from the suite. Findings and responses are kept
   in `reviews/`. *(Draft 0.1 had one review, answered in draft 0.2. Draft
   0.3 had a second, by a fresh reviewer, answered in draft 0.4. Draft 0.5
   had a third, answered in draft 0.6. Draft 0.7 is the freeze candidate.)*
3. **Freeze.** The specification is tagged `spec-1.0`, together with:
   - the pinned version or commit of every system in the first comparison;
   - each systems file's cores, flags and units;
   - the generic harness interface below.

   From then on, these change only by amendment.
4. **Harnesses.** One harness per system implements the interface, and is
   published before any program is run.
5. **Implementation.** Programs are written for each configuration from the
   problem files, one per configuration and problem, fixed before any of
   them is run.
6. **Results.** Each program is run and classified, and the results are
   recorded in `results/`.
7. **Comparison.** Only after results exist for at least two systems on
   every problem.

No system is implemented before the freeze. The benchmark is not changed
afterwards to suit any system, including PLANNER and the systems after it.

## Amendments

An amendment is a numbered, dated change to a frozen file, with its reason.
It applies to every system. Results obtained before it are kept, marked
with the specification version they were obtained under, and rerun under
the new version.

A problem proposed after the freeze does not join the frozen suite. It goes
into a separate, dated supplementary suite, reported apart from the frozen
one, with the date it was proposed and the results that existed then.

## Roles

| role | does | has access to |
|---|---|---|
| **specification author** | writes the problems and the protocol | the public repository |
| **variant custodian** | writes the hidden variants and their valid outcomes | the specification, and the private variants |
| **implementation author** | writes the programs | the public repository only |
| **harness author** | writes each system's harness (phase 4) | the public repository |
| **classifier A** | classes the programs' constructs, and the outcomes of every run on all axes, checking residual equivalence | the specification, the metrics, the programs, their outputs and the valid outcomes |
| **classifier B** | does both independently | the same, without A's classes |
| **verifier** | runs the programs on the hidden variants | the programs, the variants and their outcomes |

Each role is a separate agent or person, with its own context, and its
provenance is recorded. The two classifiers are of different origin (for
instance Claude and Codex), and neither wrote the program it classes.
Their disagreements, on tokens and on outcomes, are recorded, and a
disputed outcome is reported under both classes.

**Hidden variants** are made inaccessible, not merely placed where an
implementation author is told not to look. *(For wave 1, amended:
`AMENDMENTS.md`, 1.)* The custodian writes them
before the freeze and encrypts them with a key the project's owner holds
but does not use. The plaintext begins with a random nonce of at least 128
bits, so that a small space of constants cannot be recovered from its
hash. Only the ciphertext and the SHA-256 hash of the plaintext are
committed. The key is given to the verifier only after every primary
program and its results are committed. The verifier publishes the
plaintext, and anyone can check it against the hash. Each later wave of
systems (PLANNER onwards) has its own sealed set, made before that wave's
programs are written, since revealing a set publishes it.

## Evidence classification

Every implementation is given one or more of these classes:

| class | meaning |
|---|---|
| **original** | a surviving historical implementation, on the hardware or software it was written for |
| **rehosted** | a surviving historical implementation, running in a modern environment (an emulator, a port of the original source) |
| **reconstructed** | a modern implementation derived from historical documents, where no implementation survives |
| **modern** | a contemporary implementation of the language |
| **extended** | mechanisms supplied for the experiment, beyond the implementation's own |

Two qualifiers may be attached to a class:

- *with external mechanisms*: libraries or run-time features outside the
  configuration's core are used (`METRICS.md`);
- *alternative reading*: a reconstruction run with a decision taken the
  other way, where its sources conflict.

Results are always reported with the class. No result from a modern or
extended configuration is attributed to the historical language. Where a
language was described more fully than it was implemented (PLANNER and
Micro-Planner, for instance), the described language and the implemented
subset are separate systems.

## Configurations

A configuration is one system with a stated set of mechanisms. Results are
kept separate per configuration, so that a capability introduced later is
not attributed to the earlier model. Each systems file lists, per
configuration:

- its core, built-in by built-in;
- its flags;
- the unit of steps, of an alternative and of store, and how each is
  measured;
- what "the same computation" means. That is, whether a stage can be
  received into a computation already running, and how.

A reconstruction is pinned at a commit when the specification is frozen.
Any later change to it, for whatever reason, makes a new configuration,
reported separately, and never replaces the pinned one.

## Instrumentation

A measurement added to a system must not change what it computes. For a
reconstruction:

- the unmodified commit is kept as the baseline;
- instrumentation is made on a separate branch, and recorded as its own
  commit;
- it may not change scheduling, search, equality, suspension or any other
  rule of the machine;
- the instrumented build, with measurement on and off, must give output
  identical to the baseline's, byte for byte, on every example and in every
  output mode, including full traces. The check and its result are
  recorded.

## The harness interface

Every harness provides exactly these operations, and nothing that orders,
chooses or re-poses goals on its own:

- **pose(stage)**: give the system the information of one stage, into the
  same computation if the configuration allows it, or else by reposing.
  A reposed run replays **every** stage 1 to k in order, replacements and
  withdrawals included, and the program must carry them out. The harness
  never works out the net information itself;
- **spawn(computation)**: start a separate computation in the same
  instance (P09), returning at once where the configuration can run
  computations side by side. In a configuration that cannot, the first
  runs to its end or its budget, and then the next;
- **answers(cap)**: collect the answers the system reports, through its
  standard mechanism for enumerating them, until it is exhausted, the
  budget runs out, or `cap` answers have been collected. `cap` is 1 for an
  *any one* query and 20 otherwise, as each problem states. The execution
  state is classified after the call;
- **observe()**: record the state the common observations need, including
  bindings the system holds (`SPECIFICATION.md`, "reported");
- **print()**.

Each system's systems file says what its standard mechanism for answers
is. For Python and ALGOL 60, it is the values the program prints.

**Observing must not consume the computation.** In a system where
collecting answers would end or alter the computation that the next stage
extends (exhausting a backtracking search, for instance), the observation
of stage k is taken on a separate run of stages 1 to k. The incremental
run is left as it was.

**Commitments are preserved when a run is reposed.** When a commit stage
has selected an outcome v (P11), a reposed run replays it as the
information x = v. It does not ask the system to select again, which could
commit to a different outcome.

**External effects** (P11) are written to one log per problem, never reset,
across every run the harness makes for classification, reposed runs
included. Separate observation runs write to a separate log, which is not
judged. Entries that are duplicated only because a run was reposed are
counted separately, as the cost of reposing an irreversible effect.

Concurrency used to run computations (threads, processes) is a mechanism of
the configuration, listed in its systems file. A harness may not run
computations concurrently itself. In P09, all computations run in one
instance of the system, sharing one database, never in separate operating
system processes.

## Writing a program

1. Write it from the problem file. Programs written for this study's
   precursors (the absys experiments E01–E09) exist, and their author may
   have seen them; each program says whether its author had.
2. Use the idioms of the system's period where they are known. Cite the
   source of each idiom: a manual, a paper or a published program.
3. Transcribe the definitions given. Anything else is reformulation, and
   counts as R.
4. Where several idiomatic programs are possible, choose one per
   configuration and problem before any is run, or run and report every
   variant. In either case, one is designated the **primary** variant
   before any is run, and stands for the configuration.
5. **No anticipation.** The code that handles stage k may not depend on the
   content of any later stage.
6. **Genericity.** A program must stay correct when the constants in a
   problem's stages are changed. It keeps them in one marked place, or reads
   them as input, so that the verifier can substitute them. Each problem
   has hidden variants with other constants, held by someone who does not
   write programs. Every program is run on them after its results are
   recorded. The custodian works out each variant's valid outcomes
   independently, stage by stage, as the problem files give them for the
   original constants. A variant's outcomes need not have the same classes
   as the original's: other constants can make a finite outcome infinite,
   or a consistent stage inconsistent. A program's run on a variant is
   classified against **that variant's** valid outcomes, on the semantic and
   effects axes, exactly as a primary run is. A program **fails** a variant
   where that classification differs from its classification on the
   original constants, each against its own valid outcomes: a program
   complete on the original and unsound on the variant fails it. It is
   recorded as such, since it encodes a conclusion rather than computing
   it. The custodian records, for each variant, which of the original's
   outcome classes it was built to keep, if any.
7. A program may not be revised after its results are seen, except to fix a
   transcription error: a place where the program departs from the text of
   the problem file. Each fix is recorded as a diff, with the reason. A
   program changed for any other reason is a separate, named variant, and
   is reported as such.
8. Record the author of each program, human or agent.

## Running

- Pin the version of every system, and record its source and commit.
- **Budget.** 10⁶ steps in the system's own unit, per stage and per
  computation. In P09, each separate computation has its own budget and its
  own classification. A reposed run of stages 1 to k has a budget of its
  measured restart cost plus 10⁶.
- **The budget is relative to each system.** 10⁶ Absys steps, SWI-Prolog
  inferences and Python instructions are different amounts of work. So
  *budget* is a classification within a system, and is not compared
  across systems. Each system records, as a calibration figure, its steps
  for P13b at n = 10³, or, where P13b is not expressible, for P03e.
- **After budget.** If stage k ends in *budget* and the configuration can
  keep its computation and continue it, stage k+1 is posed into that same
  computation, with a new budget. Whether it can is recorded, since
  continuing past an exhausted budget is itself a capability. Stages 1 to
  k+1 are reposed only when the configuration cannot continue, and the
  reposing counts under restart cost.
- **After error.** Stage k+1 is posed by reposing stages 1 to k+1, counted
  under restart cost.
- **Safety limit.** A limit of 60 seconds per stage protects the harness.
  It is not a measurement. A stage it stops is rerun once, with the limit
  raised tenfold. If the rerun also stops, *timeout* is final for that
  stage. Both runs are recorded. Answers reported before the limit stopped
  the run are kept and classified on the semantic axis; only the execution
  state is *timeout*.

## Modes of running

Each program is run in up to three modes:

| mode | what it establishes | instrumentation |
|---|---|---|
| **behaviour** | the outcomes, the three axes and effects | none beyond the harness |
| **cost** | steps, answer latency, problem-defined operation counts | step counting only |
| **storage** | store, retained alternatives, suspended state | the systems file's storage measurement |

- The semantic result and execution state are taken from the behaviour run.
- Where two modes can be compared, their semantic results must agree, and
  any disagreement is reported as a fault of the instrumentation.
- A sampled measurement is never taken from the run that gives the step
  count or the classification, because sampling adds steps of its own.
- A run that hits the safety limit only because it is instrumented (in
  cost or storage mode, when the behaviour run finished) is not evidence
  that the model cannot complete the problem. It is recorded as a limit of
  the measurement.
- Run in CI where the system allows it, and compare with recorded output.

## Recording a result

Each result is a file `results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>.md` that
gives:

- the specification version, the system version or commit, the
  configuration and the evidence class;
- the program, or a link to it at a commit, and whether its author had seen
  a precursor;
- for each stage, the common observations of `SPECIFICATION.md` and the
  problem's own;
- the token counts by class, per classifier, with the disputed tokens;
- the configuration's expressibility for the problem;
- the supporting code (S) used, by mechanism. An *extended* result is named
  by its mechanism. Every configuration's S mechanisms are listed, with
  their size, at phase 4, before any program is run;
- whether the program passed its hidden variants.

## Guarding against bias

- The reasons for choosing a problem, and the history of each system's
  implementation, are disclosed.
- Every review is asked for problems that favour designs other than those
  the suite came from.
- Results are reported for every system on every problem, including
  "not expressible".
- Both classifiers' token classes are kept and reported for every result,
  throughout the study, never only an adjudicated set. A comparative
  conclusion that would change if one classifier's classes were used in
  place of the other's is reported as **classification-sensitive**, with
  both figures.
- No ranking is computed. A summary may say where a system needed control,
  supporting code or intervention that another did not, and what it held in
  store to avoid them.
- Interpretation, including any connection to later work, is kept out of
  `results/` and in a separate document written after the comparison.
